title: ‘My way to escape reality’: LensCulture street photography awards 2026 winners – in pictures
text:
‘My way to escape reality’: LensCulture street photography awards 2026 winners – in pictures
From pre-dawn Vietnam to cats scaling walls, the scenes in these prize-winning photographs show how the everyday can become mysterious, poetic and surreal
Cat’s entertainment … Levi Goldbaum’s No Body Was Cast for This Photograph: Levi Goldbaum
Vica Bogaerts: Until Dawn Comes (1st place winner, Series category)
‘When Hanoi goes to sleep, Long Biên market awakens, alive in the hours between night and first light. The market is loud, busy, chaotic. But along its quieter edges I found something else. Ordinary moments of stillness; people at work, sometimes silent, often in sync. When dawn rose over the bridge, the day’s work was done. I went home, still thinking about the market and its people. They would return the next night. Maybe I would too.’ More on the LensCulture street photography award winners. Quotes below by photographers
‘I am always trying to capture intensity and emotion through my candid street photography. Venice has been a place I’ve wanted to visit for a decade. All I had seen before were postcard photos that sell it as a holiday destination, so it was more satisfying than anywhere I’ve ever visited to dig into its reality and fill in the gaps’
Colin Helie-Harvey: Sublime Porte (1st place, Single category)
‘When we went to Istanbul to introduce our son to my wife’s family, I had the opportunity to walk around the city once again, but this time with a camera. It was an amazing experience discovering new neighbourhoods and talking with people on the street. I’ve always done this when I’m in Istanbul, but it was the first time I did it with a camera. It was a really nice experience’
‘Guiding my gaze is a search for fleeting moments through which I manage to reconcile the virtual and the real. My street photography aspires neither to journalism nor documentary. The result of my quest leads to resolutely graphic images, sometimes bordering on the abstract. The people I photograph are the main characters of their everyday lives, strong enough to leave their mark on the urban geometry of their environment. The street is a movie set where ordinary people become stars. I am just a spectator walking around with my camera’
Levi Goldbaum: No Body Was Cast for This (Juror pick)
‘Even though the photographs were taken in very different places, they seem to belong to the same strange world. Public space started to feel less like everyday reality and more like a stage: a place of entrances, pauses, gestures and silent tension’
Rattanun Rungpittaryaton: I love water, I love fish, I love cherry blossoms (Juror pick)
‘Inspired by Barry Schwartz’s The Paradox of Choice, this series explores the paradox of having too many possibilities – where more choices do not always lead to greater happiness. As children, our world was smaller. We knew less, imagined more, and did not worry about all the possibilities we might be missing. Perhaps, sometimes, we do not need more choices. Perhaps we simply need a smaller world to pause, forget our worries, and find peace in what is already in front of us’
Jirayut Thongwatcharapaiboon: After the Celebration (Juror pick)
‘In this project, I focus on spaces suspended between presence and disappearance. Ordinary environments where traces of human activity remain, though the events that preceded them are now long gone; empty parking lots, isolated urban edges, artificial landscapes, littered with abandoned decorations. Rather than documenting celebration itself, this series lingers on its aftermath’
‘These short stories, made with love, are from the alleys of Kolkata. It is an amazing experience to discover magic in the everyday, awe in the ordinary and divinity in the earthly. Kolkata is known as the ‘city of joy’. Its colours reflect the appreciation of happiness and simplicity of its people. Here, I have tried to create a narrative that infuses reality with fiction, dreams, memories, fantasies and anxieties’
‘This series was created on the suburban platforms of Madrid’s Atocha station, where a narrow shaft of sunlight appears only briefly each day, forming a stage-like spotlight. I followed not the people, but the light itself. When it touched someone in transit, a fragment emerged – a stride, a posture, a gesture – suspended between appearance and disappearance’
‘During the harsh winters of Anatolia, local children turn cold January days into a ritual, seeking warmth and joy in natural thermal waters. As they bathe their horses and buffaloes, the striking contrast between the freezing air and soothing warmth creates moments of playful delight. For these children, this place is more than a washing spot; it becomes a stage filled with fun and excitement. The series offers a glimpse into a lifestyle that thrives outside the bounds of the modern world, rooted deeply in the heart of nature’
